theme: Unit 13 review, Exile, Jeremiah, Lamentations, Ezekiel, Daniel
memoryText: I will put my law within them, and I will write it on their hearts. And I will be their God, and they shall be my people.
memoryVerseMeditation:
This is the unit’s anchor verse, the heart of the new covenant promise. After the long account of judgment, exile, and loss, it is the answer God gives to the problem of the human heart.

“I will put my law within them.” The old covenant was written on stone tablets. It was holy, righteous, and good, but it was external. The people heard it, agreed to it, and broke it. God did not change the law. He changes where it is kept. “Within them.” The law moves from tablet to the center of the person.

“And I will write it on their hearts.” To write on the heart is to make obedience a matter of desire, not just duty. It is what Ezekiel describes as a new heart and the Spirit within. Where there was resistance, there is delight. Psalm 40:8 says, “I delight to do your will, O my God; your law is within my heart.” The new covenant makes this the normal experience of God’s people.

“And I will be their God, and they shall be my people.” This is the covenant formula running through the whole Bible. It is the goal of redemption: a people who belong to God, and a God who belongs to his people. It is the language of marriage and family. It is also the language of Revelation 21:3.

Say this verse from memory, and think about the unit as a whole. It began with the fall of Jerusalem and ended with promises of a new heart, a new temple, and a kingdom that will never be destroyed. All of this is fulfilled in Jesus, who said at the Last Supper, “This cup is the new covenant in my blood.” If you have trusted in him, this promise is for you.
unitRecap: This unit covered the exile, the darkest period of the Old Testament and one of the richest in hope. Josiah’s reform could not undo Manasseh’s sin, and Jerusalem fell in 586 BC. Jeremiah, the weeping prophet, warned for forty years, confronted false hope in the temple and in false prophets, and wrote to the exiles that they should seek the welfare of Babylon. At the center of his book is the Book of Consolation, with the promise of a new covenant, in which God writes his law on the heart and forgives sin forever. Lamentations gave voice to grief and found hope in the steadfast love that is new every morning. Ezekiel saw God’s glory on a mobile throne in Babylon, watched it leave the temple, and then heard the promise of a heart of flesh, the Spirit within, the dry bones that live, and the return of the glory to a city whose name is “The LORD Is There.” Daniel showed what faithful life looks like in a foreign empire: refusing to defile himself, trusting God in the furnace and the lions’ den, and seeing the Son of Man receive an everlasting kingdom. The psalms of the unit gave words for lament, trust, and praise.

reviewQuestions.question: What is the New Covenant promise in Jeremiah 31?
reviewQuestions.prompt: Recall the four promises: the law written on the heart, a restored relationship, direct knowledge of God, and complete forgiveness. How is this different from the covenant at Sinai? Look at Hebrews 8:6-13 and Luke 22:20 to see how it is fulfilled in Christ.

reviewQuestions.question: What does the glory departing from the Temple in Ezekiel 8-11 mean?
reviewQuestions.prompt: Think about the reasons the glory left (the idolatry in the temple), the slow stages of its departure, and what it meant for the exiles. What is the significance of the glory’s return in Ezekiel 43, and how does John 1:14 relate?

reviewQuestions.question: What does Ezekiel 36-37 promise about the Spirit’s work in the New Covenant?
reviewQuestions.prompt: Consider the cleansing water, the new heart and new spirit, and the Spirit within us who causes us to walk in God’s statutes. Consider the valley of dry bones. How does Jesus’ conversation with Nicodemus in John 3:1-8 draw on this passage?

reviewQuestions.question: Who is the Son of Man in Daniel 7, and why is this title important?
reviewQuestions.prompt: Describe the scene: the beasts, the Ancient of Days, and the one like a son of man coming with the clouds. Why did Jesus use this title for himself, and why did the high priest react as he did in Mark 14:61-64?

prayerPrompts: Thank God for writing his law on your heart.
Thank him for what you have learned through the exile.
Ask him to keep the unit verse before you.
